We have a list of templates. The first one seems relevant: retro_smarts_template: '[CH2;D1;+0:1]=[C;H0;D3;+0:2](-[c:3])-[c:4]>>C-[Si](-C)(-C)-[CH2;D2;+0:1]-[Li].O=[C;H0;D3;+0:2](-[c:3])-[c:4]'

This is a retrosynthetic template: product alkene to precursor beta-hydroxy silane? Actually forward: C-[Si]... + O= C ... -> alkene. The mapped_rxn given: 'O=[C:2]([c:3]1[cH:4][cH:5][c:6]([O:7][CH3:8])[cH:9][cH:10]1)[c:11]1[cH:12][cH:13][c:14]([O:15][CH3:16])[cH:17][cH:18]1.[Li][CH2:1][Si](C)(C)C>>[CH2:1]=[C:2]([c:3]1[cH:4][cH:5][c:6]([O:7][CH3:8])[cH:9][cH:10]1)[c:11]1[cH:12][cH:13][c:14]([O:15][CH3:16])[cH:17][cH:18]1'

This matches our target product (alkene with two anisole groups). The reactants are a carbonyl (aryl ketone?) Actually O=[C:2]... is a carbonyl attached to aromatic rings (maybe a benzophenone). And LiCH2Si(C)(C)C is a silyl carbanion (trimethylsilyl). So this template is exactly Peterson elimination precursor.

Thus we need to return mapped_rxn and template_id (the integer ID used to search). The template_id is the 'template_id' field? In result dict, we have 'reaction_id' and 'template_hash', but not template_id. The problem statement says return template_id (the one used to search the database not the hash). Likely the field is 'reaction_id' or maybe there is a separate template_id not shown. In search results, each entry includes 'reaction_id' (maybe template ID). The example earlier expects integer. We'll assume template_id = reaction_id.

So for the first entry: reaction_id 1679747. mapped_rxn as given.
